full_judgment:
4. The defendant-petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the defendant petitioner filed Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gazipur stating that the suit property originally belonged to Zaminder Prashad Roy Chowdhury and Gouri Prashad Roy Chowdhury of Kashimpur Estate, PS Savar, District Dhaka belonging to Touzi No. 27. The CS record of rights was prepared in the name of Saroda Prashad Roy Chowdhury and others, the heirs of the said Gouri Prashad Roy Chowdhury, as owners in possession of land measuring 19.29 decimals of land of CS plot Nos. 440, 465, 575, 215 and 208 of CS Khatian No. 6 of the Mouja Sarabo. The Zamindary Estate of Kashimpur was divided into two Hissa i.e. 8 Annas 17 Gandas, 3 Karas, 1 Kraniti share and 7 Annas 2 Gondas 2 Kranti 2 Danti share, popularly known as 9 Annas and 7 Annas shareholders and they possessed the suit land. On the 12th Poush 1338 BS the defendant took settlement of the suit land from 9 Annas hissa and on the 7th day of Magh 1338 BS the defendant took settlement of the suit land also from the owners of 7 Annas hissa on payment of proper salami of Rs. 291.00 only and took delivery of physical possession of the suit land and is enjoying the same upon payment of rent. It is stated that the defendant being an illiterate cultivator could not get his name recorded during the SA khatian to the negligence of Jinnat Ali Moulavi of Saradaganj on whom the defendant trusted for the purpose. During the RS operation the defendant appeared before the officer who went to the locality for the purpose and after examining the defendant's papers of title, assured that the defendant's name would be duly recorded in the RS Khatian and subsequently gave an attested copy of the DP khatain No. 19 prepared in the name of the defendant but subsequently it transpired that the RS record had been prepared in the name of the plaintiff and the defendant's name was not entered therein. Hence the defendant filed the said Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur for a declaration of the defendant's-/16/-Annas right, title and interest in the suit land. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was decreed ex parte on 28-12-1981 not by suppression of summons which was duly served on 27-6-1981 and 29-6-1981 but in the presence of the Government Advocate Gazipur. The Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 for setting aside the said decree was filed on 27-3-1983 i.e. fourteen months thereafter with no.explanation or prayer for condonation of delay, therefore the Assistant Judge, Gazipur rejected the said Misc. case on contest on 28-3-1984 and the plaintiffs did not prefer any appeal therefrom. The defendant denied that he gave any undertaking that he would not possess the suit land after the dismissal of the Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 that is after the plaintiffs finally lost the case. The defendant after obtaining decree in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur started the Misc. case No. 124 of 1982 before the ADC (Rev), Dhaka which case was transferred from Dhaka to Gazipur and renumbered as Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 for correction of records in the name of the defendant. In the said Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 the learned CO Revenue, Gazipur twice conducted on the spot enquiry in the case land on visiting the suit land. The CO Revenue, Gazipur and after him the ADC (Rev), Gazipur also visited the suit land and made an on the spot enquiry and all the officers found the plaintiff to be in possession of the suit land. Thus found that this defendant was in possession of the suit land by construction of homestead, digging pond and that there was no Gazari tree or forest anywhere in the suit land. The local GP also gave his opinion that the suit land belonged to the defendant and not the plaintiff legally. Upon hearing this defendant and also because the plaintiff had no objection in the record being corrected in his name and as this defendant was in possession of the case land the ADC (Rev). Gazipur by his order dated 12-3-86 passed in Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 allowed correction of record in favour of this defendant. Thereafter there was again an on the spot survey and demarcation of the suit land by Government surveyor Mofizuddin, Revenue Department, Gazipur on 26-8-86 where the officers of the plaintiff and local Chairman were present, and the plaintiff's representative consented to the demarcation as per possession of this defendant. It was therefore submitted that the plaintiff had no right, title, and interest in the suit land and some other interested persons with ill motive started this false and frivolous suit although there was no Gazari tree anywhere in the suit land as falsely claimed in para 5 of the plaint as it appeared from the plaint. Further, none of the plaintiffs signed the plaint of the present suit. 

 7. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury, the learned Counsel appearing for the defendant-petitioner, has submitted a number of grounds whereby the appellate Court committed error of law on the face of the record leading to wrong decision and injustice on the defendant-petitioner. It is submitted that the suit land is not Gazari land and the same cannot be treated as Forest Land as had been recorded in CS Khatian No. 6 Ext. Gha in which the suit land has been described as Chala and Teek land and the schedule also supported the same. The land mentioned in the schedule of the plaint was never published in the Gazette by the Government as forest land under any provision of the Forest Act, 1927 and the learned District Judge's finding that it was forest land published in the Gazette under the provision of Forest Act, 1927 was baseless, misconceived and wrong. The only paper Ext. 1 produced by the PW 1 as notification containing some other plots than the suit plot, mere departmental notification under the provision of East Bengal Private Forest Act, 1949 and not under the provisions of Forest Act, 1927 as has been wrongly stated and observed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur. The appellate Court below committed serious error of law while reversing the finding of the trial Court that the ex parte decree having been passed upon service of summons on 28-12-1981 in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gazipur, the plaintiff opposite party preferred a Misc. case for setting aside the said ex parte decree under Order 9 rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code being Misc. case No. 26 of 1983, the restoration of the suit to its original file and number and having lost the Misc. case no. 26 of 1983 on contest on 28-3-1984 and the plaintiff-opposite party having not preferred any appeal against the said order passed in the Misc. case was debarred from filing a fresh suit between the same parties and in respect of the same property in 1987, and in not finding that the ex parte decree unless set aside also operated as res judicata in the matter. It is further submitted that a Gazette notification published on 11-7-85 and a photo copy of the same showed that the suit land was not included as forest land. A photocopy of the departmental notification dated 15-12-1953 Ext. 1 which was relied upon by the plaintiff-opposite parties was only a departmental circular and not a notification as required under section 4 of the Forest Act, 1927. It is also submitted by the learned Counsel appearing for the defendant-petitioner that the learned District Judge without considering the above facts found that the GP and the Assistant Judge had favoured the defendant petitioner who were illegally influenced by bribe and share of land. The judgment, it is submitted, is vitiated by irrelevant observation in the name of judicial notice and baseless as portion of all the concerned Government officials and the subordinate judiciary. 

 8. We will now consider the points raised by the learned Counsel for the defendant-petitioner. It appears from Ext. 'Gha' which is CS Khatian No. 6 that the suit land comprising of Plot No. 208, 215, 440 and 475 are described as Chala and Teek land. There is no mention that any of the lands was Gazari land. This has not been disputed by the plaintiffs. If these lands, were not forest land then they could not have been declared as land for reserve forest. It is the plaintiffs case that the suit land was taken over by the Government under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by Notification No. 2846 of 25-3-1953 and Notification No. 16188 of 15-12-53 and subsequently for reservation as forest under Forest Act, 1927. If it was forest land then section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act would not apply, as forest land vested in the Government without any notification of all CS recorded forest land vested in the Government as per proviso to section 20 of the Forest Act, 1927. If on the other hand the plaintiffs claim that the suit land was Gazari land is accepted, then giving notice under section 4 of Forest Act 1927 and the procedure laid down from section 4 to section 20 of the said Act has to be complied with. In the instant case although the appellate Court has referred to Gazette notification there is nothing on record to show that there was any Gazette notification under section 4 which requires there has to be a notification in the official Gazette. Ext. 1 upon which the plaintiffs have relied is a departmental notice which cannot be said to be an official notification as envisaged in section 4 of the Forest Act, 1927. In the case of Hazi Nurul Islam vs. Serajul Islam and ors. reported in 1984 BLD (AD) 36 the Appellate Division while considering the fact of Government circular in respect of principles of lease of Government fisheries held that the Matter did not have any statutory force nor were they published in the official Gazette for general information to the members of the public, so as to saddle them with the knowledge of the principles regulating the leasing out of fisheries. At best, this offered a guideline for the use of the officers of the department without prescribing any sanction against the violation of the principles contained therein as far as the members of the public are concerned.
